sentences.zh: 六月，彥超入覲，明宗召見撫諭，尋授晉州留後。

translations.literal: In the sixth month Yanchao entered court audience; Emperor Mingzong summoned him, comforted and instructed him, and soon appointed him acting governor of Jin Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month Yanchao came to court. Emperor Mingzong received him with words of comfort and soon made him acting governor of Jin Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 未行，會其弟前曹州刺史彥饒平宣武亂軍，明宗喜，召彥超謂之曰：「吾得爾兄弟力，餘更何憂，爾為我往河東撫育耆舊。

translations.literal: Before he departed, it happened that his younger brother Yanrao, former prefect of Cao, pacified the mutinous troops of Xuanyi; Emperor Mingzong was pleased, summoned Yanchao and said to him, "With your brothers' strength I have nothing more to worry over—you go for me to Hedong and nurture the elders."
translations.idiomatic: Before he could leave, his younger brother Yanrao, former prefect of Cao, pacified the mutinous Xuanyi army. The emperor was delighted and told Yanchao, "With your brothers' help I need fear nothing else. Go to Hedong for me and look after the old retainers there."

sentences.zh: 」即授北京留守、太原尹。

translations.literal: " He was at once appointed garrison commander of the Northern Capital and mayor of Taiyuan.
translations.idiomatic: " He was immediately made garrison commander of the Northern Capital and mayor of Taiyuan.

sentences.zh: 明年冬，移授昭義節度使。

translations.literal: The next winter he was transferred and appointed military commissioner of Zhaoyi.
translations.idiomatic: The following winter he was transferred to military commissioner of Zhaoyi.

sentences.zh: 四年，授驍衛上將軍，改金吾上將軍。

translations.literal: In the fourth year he was appointed general-in-chief of the Valiant Guard, then changed to general-in-chief of the Golden Crow.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of the reign he was made general-in-chief of the Valiant Guard, then reassigned as general-in-chief of the Golden Crow.

sentences.zh: 長興元年，授泰寧軍節度使，尋移鎮安州。

translations.literal: In the first year of Changxing he was appointed military commissioner of the Taiping Army, and soon transferred to garrison Anzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Changxing he was made military commissioner of Taiping, then soon transferred to garrison Anzhou.

sentences.zh: 彥超廝養中有王希全者，小字佛留，粗知書計，委主貨財，歲久耗失甚多，彥超止於訶譴而已。

translations.literal: Among Yanchao's household retainers was Wang Xiquan, childhood name Foliu, who roughly knew accounts; he was entrusted with goods and wealth, and over the years losses were very great—Yanchao only rebuked him.
translations.idiomatic: Among Yanchao's household staff was Wang Xiquan, nicknamed Foliu, who had some skill with accounts. Yanchao put him in charge of his property, but over the years enormous sums went missing, and Yanchao did no more than scold him.

sentences.zh: 應順元年正月，佛留聞朝廷多事，因與任貨兒等謀亂。

translations.literal: In the first month of the first year of Yingshun, Foliu heard the court had many troubles and therefore plotted rebellion with Ren Huo'er and others.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the first year of Yingshun, Foliu heard that the court was in turmoil and plotted a revolt with Ren Huo'er and others.

sentences.zh: 一夕，扣門言朝廷有急遞至，彥超出至廳事，佛留挾刃害之。

translations.literal: One evening he knocked at the gate saying an urgent dispatch had arrived from court; Yanchao came out to the hall, and Foliu with blade in hand killed him.
translations.idiomatic: One night he knocked at the gate and claimed an urgent dispatch had come from the capital. When Yanchao came out to the main hall, Foliu stabbed him to death.

sentences.zh: 詰旦，本州節度副使李端召州兵攻佛留等，殺之，餘眾奔淮南，擒彥超部將趙溫等二十六人誅之。

translations.literal: At daybreak the deputy military commissioner of the prefecture Li Duan summoned prefectural troops to attack Foliu and the rest, killed them, the remainder fled to Huainan, and they captured Yanchao's subordinate generals Zhao Wen and twenty-six others and executed them.
translations.idiomatic: At dawn the deputy commissioner Li Duan rallied prefectural troops against Foliu and his followers and killed them. The survivors fled to Huainan. Twenty-six of Yanchao's officers, including Zhao Wen, were captured and executed.

sentences.zh: 彥超贈太尉。

translations.literal: Yanchao was posthumously given the title of Grand Commandant.
translations.idiomatic: Yanchao was posthumously honored as Grand Commandant.

sentences.zh: 存審次子彥饒，《晉史》有傳。

translations.literal: Cunshen's second son Yanrao has a separate biography in the 《History of Jin》.
translations.idiomatic: The second son, Yanrao, is given his own biography in the 《History of Jin》.

sentences.zh: 次彥卿，曆官鳳翔節度使、守太師、中書令，封魏王，今居於洛陽。

translations.literal: Next Yanqing, who served as military commissioner of Fengxiang, held Grand Preceptor, Director of the Secretariat, was enfeoffed as Prince of Wei, and now resides at Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: Next came Yanqing, who rose to military commissioner of Fengxiang, Grand Preceptor, and Director of the Secretariat, was enfeoffed as Prince of Wei, and now lives at Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 次彥能，終於楚州防禦使。

translations.literal: Next Yanneng, who ended as defense commissioner of Chuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Next Yanneng, who ended his career as defense commissioner of Chuzhou.

sentences.zh: 次彥琳，仕皇朝為金吾上將軍，卒於任。

translations.literal: Next Yanlin, who served the imperial dynasty as general-in-chief of the Golden Crow and died in office.
translations.idiomatic: Next Yanlin, who served the present dynasty as general-in-chief of the Golden Crow and died in office.
